## 1. Written Progress Update

This week, the Web module completed the CP1 foundation for an AI question-answering experience. The repository now contains a functional chat interface, local Mock scenarios, chat and message persistence APIs, session and GitHub OAuth primitives, an AI SDK streaming route, and a Spring Boot BFF mock loop. The frontend type check, frontend lint check, and Spring Boot automated tests all pass.

citations.title: Meeting+Minutes+of+2026+09+08
citations.snippet:
osed building a more challenging question set from existing conference data.

**Discussion Summary**

- Jiajin Zhong extended OCR with visual models to analyze image content, but image description accuracy remained unsatisfactory. Vincent advise testing higher-quality visual models via API rather than local model.

- Jiaxing Dai upgraded the retrieval system to a hybrid of hierarchical navigation and knowledge layers for better long-document handling.

- Yixi Wang compared fast vs. thinking modes and found fast mode superior in both speed and quality with lower latency.

citations.title: CP1+Delivery+Summary+and+CP2+Implementation+Plan
citations.snippet:
F mock loop. The frontend type check, frontend lint check, and Spring Boot automated tests all pass.

The main focus for CP2 is integration and contract consistency rather than additional UI-only features. The current repository contains more than one chat runtime path: a browser-side Mock chat, a Nitro AI streaming route, and a Spring Boot BFF mock endpoint. CP2 will consolidate the production path, align the implementation with the latest Web Layer API specification, and make streaming, persistence, observability, and failure handling work together.

## 2. CP1 Delivered Functionality

- Message actions for copy, edit, regenerate, and helpful/not-helpful feedback.

- Chat title editing and public/private visibility controls.
